question: The particles of which metal on heating to the boiling point of 357°C go from liquid state to gas state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mercury.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__****Mercury**

__
 
• It has **relatively high surface tension**, which makes it very unique.
 
• By heating liquid mercury to its boiling point of 357°C, and under the right pressure conditions, its all particles in the liquid state go into the gas state.
 
• **The melting point **of **-38.9 Degree Celcius.**
 
• **The boiling point **of **356.7 Degree Celcius.**
 
• The only metal to remain in** liquid form at room temperature.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** Properties:

 
• **Copper**

 
 
• **​soft, malleable**, and **ductile metal with very high thermal and electrical conductivity.**
 
• A freshly exposed surface of pure copper has a **pinkish-orange colour.**
 
 
 
• **Bronze**
 
 
• **​​**It is made up of **copper and tin**, with tin accounting for roughly 12% of the alloy.
 
• It produces a **lower amount of friction** when it comes into contact with other types of metal.
 
 
 
• **Gallium**
 
 
• **​soft, silvery metal** used primarily in** electronic circuits, semiconductors and light-emitting diodes (LEDs).**
 
• It readily alloys with **most metals.**
